title: Maximize Greatness of an Array
statement: You may rearrange the values of the integer array `nums` in any order to build a new array `perm` of the same length. The *greatness* of a rearrangement is how many positions `i` satisfy `perm[i] > nums[i]`, comparing against the original, unrearranged `nums`. Return the largest greatness that any rearrangement can reach.
notes:
## Intuition

Only the multiset of values matters: each original value wants to be covered by some strictly larger value, and every value can cover at most one position. Trying all permutations is factorial. After sorting, it is best to cover the smallest values first and to use the smallest value that still beats them, so bigger values stay free for bigger targets. Scanning the sorted array as candidates while a second pointer `matched` marks the next smallest uncovered target does exactly that.

## Approach

1. Sort `nums` in ascending order.
2. Let `matched` be the number of targets covered so far; `nums[matched]` is the smallest uncovered one.
3. Walk every `value` of the sorted array from small to large.
4. If `value > nums[matched]`, it covers that target, so increase `matched`; otherwise it is too small to cover anything still open and is left for a non-scoring position.
5. Return `matched`.

## Example 1, step by step

Sorted, `nums = [1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 5]`. The three `1`s are not greater than `nums[0] = 1`. `2 > 1` gives `matched = 1`; `3 > nums[1] = 1` gives `2`; the second `3 > nums[2] = 1` gives `3`; `5 > nums[3] = 2` gives `4`. The answer is `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; the scan is O(n).
- Space: O(1) beyond the sort.

## Pitfalls

- The comparison is strict: an equal value does not count, so a run of identical numbers can never cover each other.
- `matched` never passes the current index (a value cannot beat itself), so `nums[matched]` is always in bounds.
- The answer equals `n` minus the largest count of one value; that is a handy check, but the scan shows why.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `nums` | the values, sorted ascending |
| `matched` | how many of the smallest targets are already covered |
| `value` | the candidate being placed |

narration.2: Sort so the smallest targets and the smallest candidates line up.
narration.3: No target has been covered yet; nums[matched] is the smallest open one.
narration.4: Offer each value, from smallest to largest, as a candidate.
narration.5: Is this candidate strictly bigger than the smallest uncovered target?
narration.6: Yes: it covers that target, so move on to the next one.
narration.9: Each covered target is one position where perm[i] > nums[i].
